pr_title: Update 17track integration to use v1 API
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
The old user authentication method is no longer supported. You will need to get an API token from your account settings on [17track.net](https://api.17track.net/en)

Upon receiving the token, setup the integration through the UI. 

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Updating the 17Track component to use the official V1 API instead of the no-longer supported unofficial API

New library was created, based on the old one (py17track): https://github.com/McSwindler/seventeentrack

New library matches previous spec for the most part to maintain an easy migration. Creating the client now requires a version variable, and the login method now uses token instead of username and password.

The Config Flow work was completed in #51057, but it was not merged due to conflicts. I suspect most of that PR could be salvaged and the work done here merged into it.

Thank you @rjmidau for finding that!

I'll work on updating the config flow now. I was originally going to do so in a later PR to keep things more concise, but I wasn't aware of the ADRs on that subject.

I have updated the code to include the config flow, I did end up using a lot of the code from PR [#51057](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/51057)

Looking forward to your further reviews

@frenck Is there anything outstanding on this PR which would prevent a successful re-review/merge?
I understand that there's a lot going on, but would hate to see a repeat of #51057 where it can take a long time to come back to PRs and contributors lose interest in the meantime.
Any news regarding the restored 17 Track Integration would be highly appreciated, it seems that we're very close to conquering the summit.

@engrbm87 I believe I have addressed all your comments

I am trying to test this PR on my machine but I am not able to get a token from 17track website.  I am getting permission denied when trying the url in the description.
Any idea if this api token is available to free accounts or does it require upgrading the account. As I believe the legacy authentication is still working.

> I am trying to test this PR on my machine but I am not able to get a token from 17track website. I am getting permission denied when trying the url in the description. Any idea if this api token is available to free accounts or does it require upgrading the account. As I believe the legacy authentication is still working.

Yes it is available to free accounts, but it must be a developer type account. I did not have a legacy account to test with so I am not sure if that will work or not. 

I have just repeated the steps in the doc's PR, creating a new account, and was able to get an API token without issue

I was able to create a new developer account as mentioned in the docs PR. But I couldn't find a way to switch my legacy account to the developer account. I am afraid that existing users who have legacy accounts will not be able to simply keep using their account if we switch to the token based authentication.

To my knowledge there is no way to convert an existing account to a developer account. I don't have a legacy account though, so I couldn't tell you for sure. There might be a way if you contact support.
In this case I don't think such a breaking changes will be accepted and merged. I recommend that you update the library to accept both legacy and token authentication and let the user decide.

It was my understanding that the legacy system is no longer working or at least very unstable. I don't have a legacy account to test with and say for sure though. 

Without having a legacy account myself, I don't see being able to maintain the legacy implementation.

I don't believe it doesn't make sense to support both, even temporarily.

Users who are updating Home Assistant should be reviewing the release notes and making preparations prior to updating (ie. creating a Developer account and either migrating their existing parcels in the 17track web interface, or re-creating them in Home Assistant once they have updated).

Here's our suggestion:

- Rename the existing integration to eg `17TRACK (legacy)`. Ie, change the `name` in the manifest, not the `domain`.
- Add the new API version as a new integration with a name telling it’s the main, current, integration.
- Group both integrations under the same brand. https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/creating_integration_brand/
- This will allow existing users that can use the old integration to keep using that while allowing new users to start using the new API.

issue_context.body:
### The problem

After running for a while the 17Track integration shows as Unavailable. A restart of Home Assitant fixes the problem, then after a few days it shows as Unavailable again

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.8

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

17Track

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/seventeentrack/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
#Config#
- platform: seventeentrack
  username: !secret seventeentrack_un
  password: !secret seventeentrack_pw

#Lovelace#
type: entities
entities:
  - entity: sensor.seventeentrack_packages_not_found
    name: Not Found
    secondary_info: last-updated

    secondary_info: last-updated

title: 17 Track
```

17track has released a new, official, API that I am working on integrating now. The current implementation uses an unofficial API that doesn't appear to work anymore.

Docs: https://api.17track.net/en/doc

Just a heads up, authentication will change from user/pass to an API token which you can easily get from your account dashboard.
@jmswindle is there a PR anywhere I can use to help you get this working (assuming I can find the time!)?

@proffalken finding time is always the struggle :sweat_smile:

I was originally building off of [bachya's py17track](https://github.com/bachya/py17track) but haven't gotten any response from them on my PR, so I guess I'm going to just decouple into a new library. Hopefully will have time in the next few days to get that going.
I've got a PR open, if anyone would like to test it out/review: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/70261

@McSwindler I might be able to find time to test this in the next week or so, how do I get your patch into my installation?

I'm running a version of HA in Docker, do I need to build my own container?

> @McSwindler I might be able to find time to test this in the next week or so, how do I get your patch into my installation?
> 
> I'm running a version of HA in Docker, do I need to build my own container?

Yea, I think it'd be easiest to build the image from my branch.
The old yaml config is no longer supported, you will have to setup the integration fresh through the UI. Get the API token from here: https://api.17track.net/en

@McSwindler I would gladly test it, but I cannot get the APi from 17track.

What type of 17track account were you using ?

@mimuncito looks like they've changed the sign up process since I started development, I need to update the docs to reflect this. 

- Register the account here: https://user.17track.net/en/register
- select developer account
- complete registration (phone and skype are NOT required)
- find API key here: https://api.17track.net/en/admin/settings

@McSwindler I've got the API quite fast, but I don't have the knowledge to integrate your PR into my HA core-2022.4.7 supervised version installed on a Raspberry Pi 4.

What should I do next ?

@mimuncito that I'm not sure how to do, It may be better to setup a new local environment to test, so you don't sully your existing install

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_environment/

review_comments: Please use the attribution attribute instead.
Would it work to use the account ID as default title and device name and not ask for a name here? The user can rename the config entry title and device name anyway.
Nothing is checking this return value.

We don't allow scan interval as option. Every integration that supports config entries allows the user to turn off automatic polling and then the user can automate the update interval as needed with the entity service `homeassistant.update_entity`.
Please import `device_registry.async_get` instead as normal. Using `hass.helpers` is legacy.

The code could lead to a NameError below.

Maybe it's easier to ask for the config entry id in the service call data using that selector? We support that nowadays.
Nowadays we raise `ValueError` for bad user input and `HomeAssistantError` for api call issues in service handlers. Pass a message as exception argument and it will show in the frontend.
We don't need to use an instance attribute here. Just return the dict we create from parsing the coordinator data.

Please check for the last loaded config entry instead.

Example:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6f92c5381da822dd096dc61751fa0ff49efd0816/homeassistant/components/simplisafe/__init__.py#L463-L472
Please use `DeviceInfo` when creating the device info dict.
Don't include the entity name in the unique_id. Just suffix the entity kind to the account id.
